page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 16 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz, with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes 950 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate strong memory and decompression capabilities. The instance achieved a top-tier Passmark memory score of 3332.34 and demonstrated strong memory bandwidth performance, reaching 296.76 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 130.55 GB/sec for large block write operations. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores also fell into the strong performance tier. However, LLM inference tasks represent a performance tradeoff, with text generation for small and large models scoring in the bottom 10%.

The r8gd.4xlarge offers high resource density by combining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with fast local NVMe SSD storage. This hardware profile provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive and storage-dependent workloads without requiring external block storage. The instance is highly suited for database operations, memory-cached applications, data decompression tasks, and general memory-optimized workloads, while it is less optimal for heavy LLM text generation tasks.

The r8gd.4xlarge is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, caching layers, and data processing tasks that benefit from fast local storage and high memory throughput.
